edges.description: Epithelial invasion exposes pathogen-associated ligands that recruit neutrophils and amplify ocular surface inflammation.
Severe gonococcal keratoconjunctivitis can extend from conjunctiva to the cornea, where epithelial invasion and neutrophil-mediated injury drive ulceration and stromal melt.
Neutrophil-rich conjunctival inflammation is the clinical hyperacute purulent conjunctivitis that defines ocular gonococcal disease.
Hyperacute neutrophilic inflammation with mucosal vascular injury produces the characteristic haemorrhagic conjunctivitis.
Spread of the intense surface inflammation to the adjacent eyelid tissues produces preseptal cellulitis.
Progressive stromal loss thins the infected cornea until perforation compromises globe integrity.
Keratitis and stromal collagenolysis produce the marginal or stromal corneal ulceration seen in ocular gonococcal keratoconjunctivitis.
Corneal epithelial invasion and neutrophil-mediated injury manifest clinically as keratitis.
Progressive stromal melt perforates the cornea, the vision-threatening endpoint of untreated gonococcal keratoconjunctivitis.
Contact with infected secretions deposits gonococci on conjunctival epithelium.
